data.narrative:
Forge Nano is a Series C climate and energy technology company that has raised $40M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-stage, same-sector comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—supplemented by a broader universe of nine private frontier-tech energy companies and one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implies $68M. The peer-median method, anchored to the median valuation of $1.0B across the three same-stage comparables (range: $700M–$3.0B), implies $1.0B. These divergent results reflect the structural tension in climate-tech valuations: early capital deployment versus peer multiples in a high-conviction sector.

The triangulated analysis yields a valuation range of $58M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $534M. The gap between stage-progression and peer-median methods—both applicable but yielding results 1,470% apart—reflects material uncertainty around whether Forge Nano's progress to date and competitive position merit peer-level multiples or a more conservative discount. Resolution of this gap depends on evidence regarding technology differentiation, customer traction, and path to positive unit economics relative to the named comparables.
